item: The keyword engine id is the same on Windows and Linux, and the pre-R758 Windows id of the same bytes is accepted wherever a stamp is compared, so keyword data carries between the two systems' backups and no install re-indexes
summary: Glob-matched data file names were hashed with the OS separator, so the same stoplists were a different keyword engine on Windows and a backup never carried keyword data across systems. Names are POSIX now; accepted_engine_ids/baseline_engine_ids add the old Windows id (same bytes, backslash names) and the carry plan, the carry walk, the re-index backlog and the stamp keep-or-delete accept either; only the canonical id is written. Release line: Keyword data now carries between Windows and Linux backups, so a cross-system import no longer re-indexes every article.
